title: The Final Fantasy Movie That Nearly Sank Square
hook:
Square spent 137 million dollars on The Spirits Within in 2001 and it made back about 85 million. The studio closed and the Enix merger stalled. Have you ever actually sat through it?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Final Fantasy once made a movie so expensive it nearly sank the company? In two thousand one, Square released Final Fantasy: The Spirits Within. Hironobu Sakaguchi, the creator of the series, directed it himself. It was the first photorealistic computer animated feature film. Around two hundred people spent about four years on it. Square built a whole studio in Hawaii for the project, and that building alone cost forty five million dollars. The render farm had nine hundred sixty workstations, and the average frame took ninety minutes to render. The lead character, Aki Ross, was meant to be a reusable digital actress who would star in future films. Costs kept spiraling, and by the time the film was finished the total bill had reached one hundred thirty seven million dollars. The movie earned about eighty five million dollars worldwide. Square Pictures, the studio that made the film, closed its doors in January of two thousand two, only six months after the release. A merger with Enix had been in the works for years. It was delayed because Enix hesitated to join a company that had just lost so much money. Square and Enix finally became Square Enix in two thousand three. Would you watch a new Final Fantasy movie if Square tried again? Follow for more gaming history.
